title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Property Preservation of Registered Trademark Rights by People's Courts

articles.content_en: Article 1. When a People's Court takes property preservation measures in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, if it is necessary to preserve the right to a registered trademark, it shall issue a notice of assistance in enforcement to the Trademark Office of the National Intellectual Property Administration (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Office), stating the name, registrant, registration certificate number, and preservation period of the registered trademark for which the Trademark Office's assistance in preservation is requested, as well as the contents of the assistance in enforcement, including matters such as prohibiting the assignment, cancellation of the registered trademark, modification of registration matters, and handling of pledge registration of the trademark right.

Article 2. The period of preservation of a right to a registered trademark shall not exceed one year at a time, calculated from the date on which the Trademark Office receives the notice of assistance in enforcement. If it is still necessary to continue to take preservation measures with respect to the right to the registered trademark, the People's Court shall, before the expiration of the preservation period, issue anew a notice of assistance in enforcement to the Trademark Office, requesting continued preservation. Otherwise, the property preservation of the right to the registered trademark shall be deemed to be automatically lifted.
Article 3. A People's Court shall not repeatedly conduct preservation with respect to a right to a registered trademark that has already been preserved.
